🗞 BEAT THE STREET BULLETIN 🗞

Date: 05 November 2026

Telegram: https://t.me/BeatTheStreetnews

---

📍 ORDER WIN

RAJESH POWER: Wins ₹1,628.74 Cr turnkey order from DGVCL to convert HT and LT overhead distribution networks into underground cable systems; order book rises to approximately ₹5,400 Cr.

STLNETWORK: Emerges as L1 bidder for Power Grid’s ₹555 Cr OT-SOC project covering centralised security operations for substation assets.

MARKOLINES: Secures two BMC work orders worth ₹135.20 Cr for microsurfacing and resurfacing of Eastern and Western Express Highways; unexecuted order book rises to ₹624.22 Cr.

ACCORDTS: Receives purchase orders worth ₹4.85 Cr, including a ₹4.55 Cr order from Inergy Infra for 15 transformers.

---

📍 ACQUISITION

PAJSON AGRO: Approves acquisition of 100% stake in Dubai-based Pacific Global FZCO for ₹354.52 Cr through a share swap, adding 60,000 MT cashew-processing capacity in Côte d’Ivoire; combined capacity to reach 1,13,000 MT.

RISHDIGA: SBA Infra to acquire 74.31% stake at ₹47 per share for ₹19.16 Cr and launch an open offer for the remaining 25.69% at ₹47 per share, potentially taking its holding to 100%.

KNOWLEDGE MARINE: Acquires River Pearl 48, a self-propelled trailing suction hopper dredger, to expand its fleet and strengthen capabilities in large-scale dredging projects.

NOVUS: To consider acquiring a stake in AutoPe Payment Solutions through a share swap involving 9,29,500 equity shares at its November 9 board meeting.

---

📍 FUNDRAISING

JSWDULUX: Promoter JSW Paints raises up to ₹2,950 Cr through listed NCDs to partially refinance its existing debt; JSW Dulux has no direct liability under the debenture trust deed.

SHAREINDIA: Allots 75,000 listed, rated and secured NCDs of ₹10,000 each, aggregating ₹75 Cr, through private placement.

AERONEU: Allots 48 lakh equity shares on warrant conversion and receives the balance consideration of ₹32.40 Cr.

---

📍 NEW PROJECTS

SAFARI INDUSTRIES: Approves capex of up to ₹230 Cr for manufacturing expansion; subsidiary SML to increase monthly capacity from 10 lakh to 16 lakh pieces by June 2028.

LG ELECTRONICS INDIA: Approves entry into automotive and vehicle solutions, including infotainment, digital cockpit, telematics, ADAS and automotive electronics, with manufacturing planned at its Sri City plant.

TENNIND: Approves a ₹45 Cr factory in Western India, adding approximately 3 lakh catalytic converters in phased expansion over the next 2–3 financial years.

TATA POWER: Commissions a 300 MW solar project in Karnataka for SECI, expected to generate approximately 810 million units of clean electricity annually.

MAHLIFE: Signs a development agreement for approximately 100 acres of plotted development in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, marking its entry into the segment outside Chennai.

TUBE INVESTMENTS: Approves capex of up to ₹83 Cr to enhance capacity at its existing Cold Rolled Steel Strips facility in Avadi; project expected to be completed in FY28.

---

📍 COLLABORATION

HEXAWARE: Selected as strategic technology partner by EBRD under a five-year framework covering software engineering, cloud, cybersecurity, data analytics and IT operations.

BLUECLOUDS: Signs MoU with Ghana-based Kasten Development to support marketing and implementation of its AI and enterprise technology solutions in Ghana, with potential expansion across Africa.

---

📍 Q2 / BUSINESS UPDATE

BHARAT FORGE: Q2 consolidated revenue rises 20.8% YoY to ₹4,870 Cr and EBITDA increases 8.8% to ₹778 Cr; defence order book stands at ₹10,960 Cr, with ₹2,107 Cr new orders in H1 FY27 and 20–25% FY27 India growth guidance.

M&B ENGINEERING: Q2 revenue grows 25.4% YoY to ₹384.67 Cr and PAT rises 32.8% to ₹29.49 Cr; order book reaches ₹1,109 Cr, with ₹441 Cr new orders and over 20% revenue CAGR target for the next 3–4 years.

SHILPA MEDICARE: Q2 revenue rises approximately 45% YoY and EBITDA grows 37%, with margins at 28%; API business hits a record, 20+ APIs are under development and six late-stage CDMO programmes support future growth.

CAMPUS ACTIVEWEAR: Q2 revenue increases 16.9% YoY and PAT rises 21.3%; volumes grow 10.2%, ASP increases 6.1% and women’s and kids’ segments record approximately 29% H1 volume growth.

ELECTRONICS MART INDIA: Q2 revenue grows 19% YoY, PAT surges 149% and EBITDA rises 61%; North Cluster revenue increases 45%, with SSSG at 16.5% and West Bengal expansion planned.

LOHIA CORP: Q2 order book stands at ₹1,993.6 Cr, compared with ₹1,030.7 Cr YoY; secures first South Korea order and executes specialised defence-sector machinery project.

MAHINDRA: Q2 auto business records 26% YoY SUV volume growth and retains revenue market-share leadership; EV business maintains its No. 1 position in H1, while auto PBIT margin reaches 8.8%.

MONEYBOXX: October monthly disbursements cross ₹50 Cr, more than doubling from August; AUM crosses ₹1,000 Cr and the company receives ₹144 Cr in debt funding.

SARVAMANGAL MERCANTILE: Board approves unaudited Q2 FY27 financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026.

---

📍 IPO

SHIPROCKET: Utilises ₹270.64 Cr of its ₹885.50 Cr IPO proceeds during Q2 FY27, leaving ₹614.86 Cr unutilised; ₹210 Cr used for debt repayment and ₹60.64 Cr for vendor payments.

---

📍 USFDA / REGULATORY

BHARAT PARENTERALS: Subsidiary Innoxel Lifesciences receives USFDA Establishment Inspection Report for its Vadodara injectable facility, supporting commercial supplies to the US.

DRREDDY: Receives Brazil ANVISA marketing authorisation for generic semaglutide injection, expanding its presence in the Latin American market.

POKARNA: US Department of Commerce rescinds the administrative review of anti-dumping duties on Indian quartz surface product exporters, providing greater regulatory certainty.

---

📍 LEADERSHIP CHANGES

MAXIND: Antara Senior Care appoints Dr Rachit Gulati, a Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation specialist, at its Gurugram care home.

FUSION KLASSROOM: Statutory auditor A V H P resigns citing completion of the ten-year partner association; Rao & Shyam appointed as replacement, subject to shareholder approval.

---

📍 LAUNCHES

GOLDIAM: Opens its 29th ORIGEM lab-grown diamond jewellery store at Inorbit Mall, Visakhapatnam.

MEHUL TELECOM: Opens two new franchise retail stores in Ahmedabad under the Mobile Daddy and Mehul Telecom brands.

---

📍 INCORPORATION / CORPORATE STRUCTURE

CAPACIT’E: Approves incorporation of a subsidiary in Dubai with a 75% stake, which will hold 100% in a step-down subsidiary in Uganda to undertake overseas EPC projects.

---

📍 CREDIT RATINGS

JAIN IRRIGATION: CRISIL updates bank-wise facility allocation; overall rated amount and ratings remain unchanged, with fund-based facilities at BBB-/Negative and bank guarantee/LC lines at A3.

---

📍 ADDITIONS

ADVENZYMES: Extinguishes 6,97,582 shares bought back in October 2026; paid-up capital reduces to 10,95,65,244 equity shares of ₹2 each.

---

📍 IT NEWS

GNG ELECTRONICS: TeamGroup warns that the memory shortage has not peaked, with the worst chip shortage expected from Q4 2026 through Q2 2027.

STERLITE TECH, HFCL, THERMAX, GE T&D, AEROFLEX IND: US data-centre buildout faces permitting, power and construction delays; only 25–30 GW of proposed 2027 capacity may become operational, while AI computing demand remains strong.

---

📍 OTHERS

BERNSTEIN ON AI INFRASTRUCTURE: Estimates a $750 Bn infrastructure opportunity linked to OpenAI commitments, but warns that GPU oversupply and normalisation of supply-demand could pressure rental rates within 2–3 years.

NUVAMA ON FMCG: Falling crude prices could support margin recovery and volume growth; top fundamental picks include Pidilite, Marico, Tata Consumer and United Breweries.

GALLANTT ISPAT: Promoter group shareholders to transfer 80 lakh shares, representing 3.376% stake, through an inter-se transfer; no open offer triggered and total promoter holding remains 71.464%.

LENSKART – HSBC: Upgrades to Buy with target price of ₹790, citing strong India same-store sales growth and international business momentum.

LENSKART – MACQUARIE: Maintains Outperform with target price of ₹750; highlights stronger-than-expected EBITDA growth, store additions and AI-led eye-testing opportunity.

LENSKART – NOMURA: Maintains Buy with target price of ₹888; Q2 sales grow 32.5% and EBITDA rises 65% YoY, supported by operating leverage.

APTUS VALUE HOUSING FINANCE – CITI: Maintains Buy but cuts target price to ₹285 from ₹350, citing slower AUM growth and higher funding costs.

EXIDE INDUSTRIES – CITI: Maintains Buy with target price of ₹560, citing the 6 GWh Bengaluru lithium-ion cell facility and strong automotive demand.

DR LAL PATHLABS – NOMURA: Maintains Buy with target price of ₹2,280 after a strong Q2 performance; estimates FY27 revenue growth of 18.7% and EBITDA margin of 29.4%.

PFIZER INDIA – BERNSTEIN: Maintains Outperform with target price of ₹4,424, citing specialty medicines, hospital-focused therapies and improving operating leverage.

ABBOTT INDIA – BERNSTEIN: Maintains Market-Perform with target price of ₹24,851; established brands support growth, while a limited new-molecule pipeline remains a constraint.

EMMVEE PHOTOVOLTAIC POWER – JEFFERIES: Maintains Buy with target price of ₹430; expects domestic solar module demand of 70 GW in FY27 and projects 34% EBITDA CAGR through FY29.

ANTHEM BIOSCIENCES – JEFFERIES: Maintains Buy with target price of ₹1,050; expects late-stage molecules to move into commercial manufacturing and plans ₹1,200 Cr capex.

ENDURANCE TECHNOLOGIES – GOLDMAN SACHS: Maintains Neutral and cuts target price to ₹2,650 from ₹3,090, citing near-term cost pressures and lower earnings estimates.

ENDURANCE TECHNOLOGIES – KOTAK: Maintains Add and cuts target price to ₹2,825 from ₹3,000; sees long-term growth from EV components and diversification into aerospace and defence.

VARROC ENGINEERING – KOTAK: Maintains Reduce with target price of ₹740, citing subdued margin recovery and pricing pressure despite EV-related growth opportunities.

LUPIN – KOTAK: Maintains Add with target price of ₹2,335; India formulations expected to outperform, while US competition may pressure near-term profitability.

BOFA ON INDIA EQUITY STRATEGY: Says India could benefit from lower AI exposure, weaker US dollar and potential FII inflows, while expensive AI-capex exporters and industrial names may face risks from slower data-centre orders.

---

• SPV formed for development of transmission system for power evacuation of 4000 MW through STU network from proposed thermal power plants in Madhya Pradesh
• PFC Consulting acts as Bid Process Coordinator for independent transmission projects under Ministry of Power tariff based competitive bidding guidelines
• SPV will handle preparatory activities such as survey, report preparation, land acquisition initiation and forest clearance, then be transferred to the successful bidder through international competitive bidding

Impact: Neutral (routine SPV incorporation for a transmission project; no deal value or earnings impact disclosed)

text:
**Arvind Fashions

A few interesting commitments:

→ Mid-double-digit revenue growth for the balance of FY27
→ 30–40 bps EBITDA margin expansion
→ D2C share target of ~65%, from 53% currently
→ H2 free cash flow release of ₹150–175 crore, with a large part intended for debt reduction.
Growth, channel mix and balance-sheet improvement. Worth tracking together.**

**Carborundum Universal Q2

A good example of why segment-level analysis matters.

FY27 guidance:

→ Ceramics growth raised to 25–28%
→ Ceramics margin raised to 22.5–23.5%
→ Abrasives margin lowered to 8–8.5%.
Different segments, different trajectories. Consolidated numbers may not tell the complete story.**

**Tanfac Industries Q2

Management raised FY27 revenue growth guidance from 30% to 35–40%.

The bigger story is HFC-32:

→ 2,000–3,000 tonnes volume ramp-up in FY27
→ ~95% utilisation targeted in FY28
→ FY28 EBITDA margin guidance: 24–26%.
A significant capacity ramp-up lies ahead.**

**Dhoot Transmission Q2 

Strong growth ambitions:

→ FY27 revenue growth: 40–45%
→ FY27 capex: ~₹750 crore
→ EBITDA margin: 15–16%
→ Three additional wiring harness plants expected by mid-FY28.
Now, execution and utilisation will be key to watch.**

**GNG Electronics

Management raised its FY27 revenue growth guidance to ~40%.
PAT margin expansion guidance also improved from 100 bps to 150 bps over FY26.
One thing to watch: inventory is expected to remain elevated through Q4 FY27.**

**PRABHUDAS LILLADHER – INDRAPRASTHA GAS (IGL)**

**Rating & Target Price**
- Rating: Buy.
- Target price revised to ₹161 from ₹165.

**Q2 FY27 Performance**
- EBITDA loss: ₹30 Cr.
- EBITDA missed estimates significantly.
- EBITDA/scm: -₹0.30 vs ₹3.40 in Q1.
- Gas costs increased 22% QoQ, 47.9% YoY.

**Volume Performance**
- Total volumes: 10.1 mmscmd, up 8% YoY.
- CNG volumes: 7.6 mmscmd, up 8.7%.
- PNG volumes: 2.5 mmscmd, up 6%.
- Total volumes grew 4.2% QoQ.

**Margin & Supply Outlook**
- Spot LNG share increased to 15% from 3%.
- Management retains ₹6–7/scm EBITDA guidance.
- Term LNG supplies expected from Q3.
- Further supply additions expected during Q4.
- Targets approximately 10% volume growth.

**Valuation**
- Standalone business valued at 10x Sep'28E EPS.
- Investments valued at ₹21/share.
- Holding company discount: 25%.

**Key Takeaway**
- Higher spot gas costs severely impacted margins.
- Strong volume growth remains encouraging.
- Term LNG recovery is the key catalyst.
- Impact: **Mixed to Positive**

Curious when FII will come back to India

So gave Co-pilot a prompt
“Why FIIs wont return to India even as AI trade unwind globally”

Reverse Psychology

Here is the response

1. India is still expensive vs EM peers
o Even after corrections, India trades at a premium to most emerging markets.
o FIIs compare India with China, Korea, Taiwan, Brazil, not with India's own history.
o If China is at 10-12x PE and India at 20-25x PE, capital tends to chase cheaper markets. 
2. India lacks direct AI beneficiaries
o The AI trade created winners in US tech, Taiwan semiconductors and Korean memory-chip companies.
o India has very few large listed AI, semiconductor or hyperscaler plays that global thematic funds can buy. 
3. Dollar returns matter, not rupee returns
o FIIs think in USD.
o Even if Nifty is flat or slightly up, rupee depreciation can wipe out returns.
o Currency risk remains a major deterrent for foreign capital. 
4. US yields remain a strong competitor
o If US Treasuries offer attractive risk-free returns, FIIs need a much higher expected return from India.
o Many global allocators prefer earning 4-5% in dollar assets rather than taking EM risk. 
5. India's earnings growth has moderated
o India's premium valuation was justified when earnings were compounding rapidly.
o If earnings growth slows while valuations remain rich, FIIs question the risk-reward. 
6. Better opportunities elsewhere
o Korea, Taiwan and China offer exposure to AI, semiconductors and manufacturing at lower valuations.
o Global funds have finite capital; India is competing against these markets for allocation. 
7. India is no longer an under-owned market
o After years of strong inflows, most EM funds already have meaningful India exposure.
o Incremental flows require a new catalyst, not just the absence of AI enthusiasm.
8. Domestic flows reduce urgency
o SIPs, mutual funds and insurance money continue supporting Indian markets despite FII selling.
o Paradoxically, this resilience prevents large valuation corrections that would otherwise attract FIIs back.

Maruti Suzuki India should be rechristened as Suzuki India

Maruti's journey started as a Govt of India project. Maruti Udyog was the Indian promoter & Suzuki was brought in as the technology partner. Back then, this was very much an Indian company with Japanese know-how.

Over time, the Indian promoter gradually diluted its holding & eventually exited completely. Suzuki did the opposite, staying invested through every cycle & steadily increasing its stake.

What began as a JV slowly became Suzuki's most important global asset. The ownership story itself tells you who has deepened commitment over the decades.

For years, investors debated why Suzuki was setting up fresh manufacturing capacity outside Maruti Suzuki through its Gujarat subsidiary instead of housing it directly in the listed entity.

Then came the reversal. Suzuki transferred Suzuki Motor Gujarat into Maruti Suzuki at a valuation of roughly ₹12,000+ Cr. Rather than taking cash, it largely took equity.

The result? Suzuki's ownership in Maruti Suzuki moved up further without having to buy equivalent shares from the secondary market.

This wasn't just a restructuring exercise. It was Suzuki effectively converting manufacturing assets into a larger stake in India's largest PV company.

Even after that transaction, Suzuki did not stop. It has periodically picked up additional shares from the open market whenever opportunities emerged.

The message is clear. The Indian promoter exited long ago. The Japanese promoter keeps doubling down on India.

Look at the cars on the road today. The branding emphasis is on the giant "S" logo. 10-15years back, cars started selling with only “S” logo, 1st on premium nexa cars, then on all the models. You will hardly see Maruti branded cars on road now

For many younger buyers, the brand recall is shifting from "Maruti Suzuki" to simply "Suzuki". The transition is subtle but visible.

India is now the crown jewel of Suzuki Motor Corp. A substantial portion of Suzuki valuation come from Indian listed entity. Maruti $38bn mcap translate to $21bn (for 58% stake, $15bn if applied 30% Holdco disc).

Even beyond that, Maruti pays over $500m to Suzuki as royalty, that value must be over $5bn in the SoTP of Suzuki motors. Suzuki motors also have successful 2w biz in India, they are 6th largest 2w in India, clocking over 1lac units every month

In many ways, investors buying Suzuki Motor Corp are indirectly buying the India story. Cars sold by Suzuki in India is higher than overall car sold by Suzuki in other 100 countries combined

A rebranding to "Suzuki India" could also help shed the old "cheap small-car company" perception. As premium SUVs, hybrids & future EVs gain share, a stronger global MNC identity may command a different customer mindset.

Ownership, capital allocation, manufacturing integration, branding & growth strategy all point in one direction: this is increasingly Suzuki's India story.

Conclusion: Maruti only stays in Co. name hence should be renamed now
